##### 5.1.10.7 ModifyImageSharePermission

Manages the share permission on a custom image. After you share a custom image to another Apsara Stack tenant account, the account can use the shared image to create Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances (RunInstances) or replace the system disks of ECS instances (ReplaceSystemDisk). When you call this operation, take note of the following items: You can share only your own custom images to other Apsara Stack tenant accounts. A custom image can be shared to up to 10 Apsara Stack tenant accounts at a time. You can specify up to 10 Apsara Stack tenant account IDs in the AddAccount.N or RemoveAccount.N parameter. If you specify more than 10 account IDs, the parameter is ignored. A single custom image can be shared to up to 50 Apsara Stack tenant accounts. If an instance was created (RunInstances) from a shared image, the system disk of this instance cannot be re-initialized (ReInitDisk) after the image owner unshares or deletes the image (DeleteImage).

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Require d | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | ModifyImageShar ePermission | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to ModifyImageSharePermission. |
| ImageId | String | Yes | m-imageid1 | The ID of the custom image. |
| RegionId | String | Yes | cn-qingdao- env17-d01 | The region ID of the custom image. You can call the DescribeRegions operation to query the most recent region list. |
| AddAccount.N | RepeatLi st | No | 155780923*** | The ID of Apsara Stack tenant account N to which to share the custom image. Valid values of N: 1 to 10. If the value of N is greater than 10, this parameter is ignored. |
| RemoveAccount. N | RepeatLi st | No | 155780923*** | The ID of Apsara Stack tenant account N to which to unshare the custom image. Valid values of N: 1 to 10. If the value of N is greater than 10, this parameter is ignored. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| RequestId | String | 473469C7-AA6F- 4DC5-B3DB- A3DC0DE3C83E | The ID of the request. |

**Examples**


##### 5.1.10.9 ImportImage

Imports an image to Elastic Compute Service (ECS). The imported image exists as a custom image in the destination region. You can use the imported image to create ECS instances (RunInstances) or replace the system disks of ECS instances (ReplaceSystemDisk).

**Usage notes**

When you call this operation, take note of the following items: Before you can import an image, you must upload the image to an Object Storage Service (OSS) bucket. Before you import images for the first time, you must use Resource Access Management (RAM) to authorize ECS to access your OSS buckets. If ECS is not authorized to access your OSS buckets, the `NoSetRoletoECSServiceAcount` error code is returned. The following example shows some steps in the authorization procedure: i. Create a role named `AliyunECSImageImportDefaultRole` . You must use this exact role name. Otherwise, the image cannot be imported. Configure the following trust policy for the role: `{`

```json
  "Statement": [
```

`{`

```json
      "Action": "sts:AssumeRole",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {
        "Service": [
          "ecs.example.com"
```

`]` `}` `}` `],`

```json
  "Version": "1"
```

`}` ii. Attach the `AliyunECSImageImportRolePolicy` system policy to the role. You can also create a custom policy that contains the following content and attach the policy to the role: `{`

```json
  "Version": "1",
  "Statement": [
```

`{`

```json
      "Action": [
       "oss:GetObject",
        "oss:GetBucketLocation",
        "oss:GetBucketInfo"
```

`],`

```json
      "Resource": "*",
      "Effect": "Allow"
```

`}` `]` `}` You cannot delete an image that is being imported. However, you can call the CancelTask operation to cancel the image import task. After the image import task is canceled, the image imported by the task is deleted. You can import an image only to the same region as the OSS bucket to which the image file is uploaded. The valid values of N in `DiskDeviceMapping.N` range from 1 to 17. When N is set to 1, the disk is a system disk. When N is set to a value from 2 to 17, the disk is a data disk. If the image that you want to import uses the ARM64 architecture, you must configure the realtime clock (RTC) to use the Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) time standard.

Note Before you import images for the first time, you must use RAM to authorize ECS to access your OSS buckets. ##### 5.1.11.2 AttachClassicLinkVpc

Links an instance that is deployed in the classic network to a virtual private cloud (VPC) by establishing a ClassicLink connection between the classic network and the VPC. This way, the instance can communicate with cloud resources in the VPC over the internal network. When you call this operation, take note of the following items: The instance that you want to connect to a VPC must be in the **Running** or **Stopped** state. The instance and the VPC must reside in the same region.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Require d | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | AttachClassicLink Vpc | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to AttachClassicLinkVpc. |
| InstanceId | String | Yes | i-test | The ID of the instance that is deployed in the classic network. You can call the DescribeInstances operation to query all the available instances. |
| RegionId | String | Yes | cn-qingdao- env17-d01 | The region ID of the instance. You can call the DescribeRegions operation to query the most recent region list. |
| VpcId | String | Yes | vpc-test | The ID of the VPC for which the ClassicLink feature is enabled. You can call the DescribeVpcs operation to query all the available VPCs. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| RequestId | String | 473469C7-AA6F- 4DC5-B3DB- A3DC0DE3**** | The ID of the request. |

Sample requests

##### 5.1.11.3 ModifyInstanceSpec

Changes the instance type and network bandwidth of an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance.

**Usage notes**

Before you call this operation, take note of the following items: You can change the network bandwidth of an ECS instance only when the instance is in the Running or Stopped state. Before you change the instance type of an ECS instance, you can call the DescribeResourcesModification operation to query the instance types to which you can change. You can change the instance type of an ECS instance only when the instance is in the Stopped state. You can change either the instance type or the network bandwidth of an instance at a time. After you change the instance type or network bandwidth of an instance, you cannot change the instance again within 5 minutes.

##### 5.1.11.4 DescribeClassicLinkInstances

You can call this operation to query one or more classic network-type instances that are linked to VPCs. When you call this operation, take note of the following items: This operation applies only to instances in the classic network. You can query a maximum of 100 classic network-type instances each time. At least one of VpcId and InstanceId must be specified.

#### 5.1.12 Security groups

##### 5.1.12.1 CreateSecurityGroup

Creates a security group. By default, a security group allows mutual access between instances in the security group. Access requests to the security group from outside are denied. If you want to allow requests from the Internet or requests from instances in other security groups, you can call the AuthorizeSecurityGroup operation. Usage notes To create a security group of the Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) type, you must specify `VpcId` .

##### 5.1.12.2 AuthorizeSecurityGroup

Creates an inbound security group rule. You can use the created rule to allow or deny inbound traffic from other devices to instances in the security group.

**Operation description**

In security group-related API documents, traffic is sent from the source to the destination. When you call this operation, note the following: The total number of inbound and outbound security group rules cannot exceed 1,000. The valid values of the Priority parameter range from 1 to 100. A smaller value indicates a higher priority. When multiple security group rules have the same priority, drop rules take precedence. The source devices can belong to a specified range of IP addresses (SourceCidrIp) or can be Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances in another security group (SourceGroupId). If the security group rule that you want to create already exists, no rule is created when the AuthorizeSecurityGroup operation is called. You can determine a security group rule by specifying one of the following groups of parameters. You cannot determine a security group rule by specifying only one parameter. Parameters used to specify an inbound security group rule that controls access from a specific CIDR block: IpProtocol, PortRange, SourcePortRange (optional), NicType, Policy, and SourceCidrIp. For a security group in the classic network, you can set the NicType parameter to internet or intranet. For a security group in a virtual private cloud (VPC), you must set the NicType parameter to intranet. Sample request:

```
https://ecs.example.com/?Action=AuthorizeSecurityGroup &SecurityGroupId=sg-F876FF7** &SourceCidrIp=10.0.0.0/8 &IpProtocol=tcp &PortRange=22/22 &NicType=intranet &Policy=accept &<Common request parameters>
```

Parameters used to specify an inbound security group rule that controls access from a security group: IpProtocol, PortRange, SourcePortRange (optional), NicType, Policy, SourceGroupOwnerAccount, and SourceGroupId. In this case, you must set NicType to intranet. For mutual access between security groups in the classic network, you can allow or deny another security group within the same region access to your security group. The security group that is allowed access to your security group can belong to your own Alibaba Cloud account or another Alibaba Cloud account specified by the SourceGroupOwnerAccount parameter. For mutual access between security groups in VPCs, you can allow or deny another security group within the same VPC access to your security group. Sample request:

```
https://ecs.example.com/?Action=AuthorizeSecurityGroup &SecurityGroupId=sg-F876FF7** &SourceGroupId=sg-1651FBB** &SourceGroupOwnerAccount=t***@aliyun.com &IpProtocol=tcp &PortRange=22/22 &NicType=intranet &Policy=drop &<Common request parameters>
```

**Request headers**

The AuthorizeSecurityGroup operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see Common request headers.

**Request parameters**

| Paramet er | Type | Positi on | Require d | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

##### 5.1.12.3 AuthorizeSecurityGroupEgress

Creates an outbound rule in a security group. You can use the created rule to allow or deny outbound traffic from instances in the security group to other devices.

**Operation description**

In security group-related API documents, traffic is sent from the source to the destination. When you call this operation, you need to understand the following information: The total number of inbound and outbound rules in a security group cannot exceed 1,000. For each security group rule, you can set Policy to accept or drop to specify whether to allow or deny access. The valid values of the Priority parameter range from 1 to 100. A smaller value indicates a higher priority. When several security group rules have the same priority, drop rules take precedence. The destination can be a CIDR block (DestCidrIp) or ECS instances in another security group (DestGroupId). If the rule that you want to create matches an existing rule, the AuthorizeSecurityGroupEgress operation is successful but no rule is created. You can determine a security group rule by specifying one of the following groups of parameters. You cannot determine a security group rule by specifying only one parameter. Parameters used to specify an outbound security group rule that controls access to a specified CIDR block: IpProtocol, PortRange, SourcePortRange (optional), NicType, Policy, and DestCidrIp.

```
https://ecs.example.com/?Action=AuthorizeSecurityGroupEgress &SecurityGroupId=sg-bp67acfmxazb4ph*** &IpProtocol=icmp &DestCidrIp=10.0.0.0/8 &PortRange=-1/-1 &NicType=intranet &Policy=Allow &RegionId=cn-qingdao-env17-d01 &<Common request parameters>
```

Parameters used to specify an outbound security group rule that controls access to another security group: IpProtocol, PortRange, SourcePortRange (optional), NicType, Policy, DestGroupOwnerAccount, and DestGroupId.

```
https://ecs.example.com/?Action=AuthorizeSecurityGroupEgress &SecurityGroupId=sg-bp67acfmxazb4ph*** &DestGroupId=sg-bp67acfmxazb4pi*** &DestGroupOwnerAccount=T***@aliyun.com &IpProtocol=tcp &PortRange=22/22 &NicType=intranet &Policy=Drop &RegionId=cn-qingdao-env17-d01 &<Common request parameters>
```

##### 5.1.12.4 JoinSecurityGroup

Adds an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance to a security group.

**Usage notes**

When you call this operation, take note of the following items: You can add an ECS instance to a security group only when the instance is in the `Stopped` or `Running` state. An ECS instance can be added to up to 10 security groups. Each security group can contain up to 1,000 ECS instances. The security group and the ECS instance to be added to the security group must reside in the same region. The security group and the ECS instance must be of the same network type. For example, if the network type is Virtual Private Cloud (VPC), the security group and the ECS instance must be in the same VPC.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request parameters" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Request parameters**

| Paramet er | Type | Positi on | Require d | Example | Description |

| Action | String | Query | Yes | JoinSecurityGroup | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to JoinSecurityGroup. |
| SecurityGr oupId | String | Query | Yes | sg-bp67acfmxazb4ph*** | The ID of the security group. You can call the DescribeSecurityGroups operation to query the latest security group list. |
| InstanceId | String | Query | No | i-bp67acfmxazb4ph*** | The ID of the ECS instance to be added to the security group. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| RequestId | String | 473469C7-AA6F- 4DC5-B3DB- A3DC0DE3C83E | The request ID. |

##### 5.1.12.5 LeaveSecurityGroup

You can call this operation to remove an ECS instance from a security group. When you call this operation, take note of the following items: Before you remove an ECS instance from a security group, make sure that the instance is in the
**Stopped** (Stopped) or **Running** (Running) state.
An instance must belong to at least one security group. Therefore, if the instance to be removed belongs to only a single security group, the LeaveSecurityGroup request fails.

| SecurityGroupId | String | Yes | sg- bp67acfmxazb4p h*** | The ID of the security group. |

##### 5.1.12.6 DeleteSecurityGroup

You can call this operation to delete a security group. Before you delete a security group, make sure that no instances exist in the security group and that the security group is not referenced by rules of other security groups. Otherwise, the DeleteSecurityGroup request fails. You can call the DescribeSecurityGroupReferences operation to check whether the security group is referenced by rules of other security groups.

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

##### 5.1.12.8 DescribeSecurityGroups

Queries the basic information about security groups. The basic information about security groups includes their IDs and descriptions. In the response, security groups are displayed in descending order of their IDs. When you use Alibaba Cloud CLI to call an API operation, you must specify request parameters of different data types in required formats.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Require d | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| Action | String | Yes | DescribeSecurity Groups | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to DescribeSecurityGroups. |

| PageNumber | Integer | No | 1 | The number of the page to return. Pages start from page 1. Default value: 1. |
| PageSize | Integer | No | 10 | The number of entries to return on each page. Maximum value: 50. Default value: 10. |

##### 5.1.12.9 DescribeSecurityGroupReferences

You can call this operation to query whether one or more security groups are referenced by rules of other security groups. When you call this operation, take note of the following items: Security group-level authorization includes authorization for inbound and outbound traffic. A maximum of 100 entries can be returned each time. If you fail to delete a security group by calling the DeleteSecurityGroup operation, you can call the DescribeSecurityGroupReferences operation to check whether the security group is referenced by rules of other security groups. If the security group is referenced by a rule of another security group, you must remove the reference before you can delete the security group.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Require d | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | DescribeSecurity GroupReferences | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to DescribeSecurityGroupReferences. |
| RegionId | String | Yes | cn-qingdao- env17-d01 | The region ID of the security group. |
| SecurityGroupId. N | RepeatLi st | Yes | sg- bp1euoep32o6kv rw**** | The ID of security group N. Valid values of N: 1 to 10. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| RequestId | String | 473469C7-AA6F- 4DC5-B3DB- A3DC0DE3C83E | The ID of the request. |
| SecurityGroupR eferences | Array of SecurityGroupR eference |   | Details about the references to the specified security groups. |
| SecurityGroupR eference |   |   |   |

| ReferencingSec urityGroups | Array of ReferencingSec urityGroup |   | Details about the security groups whose rules are referencing the specified security groups. |
|---|---|---|---|
| ReferencingSec urityGroup |   |   |   |
| AliUid | String | 1557809237** | The ID of the Apsara Stack tenant account to which the security group belongs. |
| SecurityGroupI d | String | sg- bp1euoep32o6kvrw **** | The ID of the security group whose rules reference the specified security group |
| SecurityGroupI d | String | sg- bp67acfmxazb4pj** ** | The ID of the specified security group. |

##### 5.1.12.10 RevokeSecurityGroup

Deletes an inbound security group rule. After the rule is deleted, the access control implemented by the rule is removed. In the security group-related API documents, inbound traffic refers to the traffic sent by the source and received by the destination. You can delete a specific inbound rule by specifying one of the following groups of parameters. However, you cannot delete the security group rule by specifying only one of the parameters in a group. Parameters used to specify an inbound security group rule that controls access from specified ranges of IP addresses: IpProtocol, PortRange, SourcePortRange (optional), NicType, Policy, DestCidrIp, and SourceCidrIp (optional). Parameters used to specify an inbound security group rule that controls access from a specified security group: IpProtocol, PortRange, SourcePortRange (optional), NicType, Policy, DestCidrIp (optional), DestGroupOwnerAccount, and DestGroupId. If the security group rule to be deleted does not exist, the RevokeSecurityGroup operation succeeds but no rule is deleted.

**Request headers**

##### 5.1.12.11 RevokeSecurityGroupEgress

Call RevokeSecurityGroupEgress operation to delete an outbound security group rule. After the rule is deleted, the access permission implemented by the rule is removed.

**Operation description**

In the security group-related API documents, traffic is sent from the source (Source) to the destination (Dest). You can determine a security group rule by specifying one of the following groups of parameters. You cannot determine a security group rule by specifying only one parameter. Revoke access permissions for a specified CIDR block, such as following requests: IpProtocol, PortRange, (Optional) SourcePortRange, NicType, Policy, DestCidrIp, and (Optional) SourceCidrIp.

```
https://ecs.example.com/?Action=RevokeSecurityGroupEgress &SecurityGroupId=sg-bp67acfmxazb4ph*** &IpProtocol=tcp &DestCidrIp=10.0.0.0/8 &PortRange=-22/22 &NicType=intranet &Policy=Allow &<Common request parameters>
```

Revoke access permissions for other security groups, such as following requests: IpProtocol, PortRange, (Optional) SourcePortRange, NicType, Policy, (Optional) DestCidrIp, DestGroupOwnerAccount, and DestGroupId.

```
https://ecs.example.com/?Action=RevokeSecurityGroupEgress &SecurityGroupId=sg-bp67acfmxazb4ph*** &DestGroupId=sg-bp67acfmxazb4pi*** &DestGroupOwnerAccount=t***@aliyun.com &IpProtocol=tcp &PortRange=22/22 &NicType=intranet &Policy=Drop &<Common request parameters>
```

If the matched security group rule does not exist, this RevokeSecurityGroupEgress call succeeds but no rule is deleted.

##### 5.1.12.13 ModifySecurityGroupPolicy

Modifies the internal access policy of a basic security group. The internal access policies of advanced security groups cannot be modified.

**Usage notes**

Take note of the following items: When InnerAccessPolicy is set to Accept for a security group, the instances in the security group can communicate with each other. The Accept internal access policy takes precedence over user-created security group rules to keep instances in the security group accessible to each other. When InnerAccessPolicy is set to Drop for a security group, the instances in the security group are isolated from each other. User-created security group rules take precedence over the Drop internal access policy and can allow access between the instances. For example, you can call the AuthorizeSecurityGroup operation to create an inbound security group rule that allows the instances in the security group to communicate with each other. You can call the DescribeSecurityGroupAttribute operation to query the internal access policy of a security group.

**Request parameters**

|---|---|---|---|---|

|---|---|---|---|---|
| InnerAccessPolicy | String | Yes | Drop | The internal access policy of the security group. Valid values: Accept Drop The value of this parameter is case- insensitive. |
| RegionId | String | Yes | cn-qingdao- env17-**** | The region ID of the security group. You can call the DescribeRegions operation to query the most recent region list. |
| SecurityGroupId | String | Yes | sg- bp67acfmxazb4p h*** | The ID of the security group. |
| ClientToken | String | No | 123e4567-e89b- 12d3-a456- 426655440000 | The client token that is used to ensure the idempotence of the request. You can use the client to generate the token, but you must make sure that the token is unique among different requests. The token can contain only ASCII characters and cannot exceed 64 characters in length. For more information, see the "How to ensure idempotence" topic in the ECS Developer Guide. |

**Response parameters**

|---|---|---|---|
| RequestId | String | CEF72CEB-54B6- 4AE8-B225- F876FF7***** | The request ID. |

##### 5.1.12.14 ModifySecurityGroupRule

Calls ModifySecurityGroupRule to modify an inbound security group rule in a specified security group. Operation description When modifying a security group rule by specifying the security group rule ID, consider the following limitations: The authorization objects of security group rules can be IPv4 CIDR blocks (or IP addresses), IPv6 CIDR blocks (or IP addresses), or security groups. You cannot change the authorization object type of an existing security group rule using this operation. For example, if the original authorization object type is an IPv4 CIDR block, you can change it to another IPv4 CIDR block (or IP address), but you cannot change it to an IPv6 CIDR block (or IP address) or a security group. You cannot delete the value of a non-empty parameter. If you want to delete the values of nonempty parameters, we recommend that you create a new rule and delete the original rule.

#### 5.1.13 SSH key pairs

##### 5.1.13.1 CreateKeyPair

You can call this operation to create an SSH key pair. Apsara Stack stores the public key and returns the unencrypted private key. The private key is PEM-encoded in the PKCS#8 format. You must securely lock away the private key on your own. In addition to calling CreateKeyPair, you can create a key pair by using other key pair generation tools and call ImportKeyPair to upload the key pair to a region. You have a maximum of 500 key pairs in each region.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Require d | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | CreateKeyPair | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to CreateKeyPair. |
| KeyPairName | String | Yes | TestKeyPairV23 | The name of the key pair. The name must be 2 to 128 characters in length. It must start with a letter and cannot start with http:// or https. The name can contain letters, digits, colons (:), underscores ( ), and hyphens (-). _ |
| RegionId | String | Yes | cn-qingdao- env17-d01 | The ID of the region in which to create the key pair. You can call the DescribeRegions operation to query the most recent region list. |
| Tag.N.Key | String | No | TestKey | The key of tag N to be bound to the key pair. Valid values of N: 1 to 20. The tag key cannot be an empty string. It can be up to 128 characters in length and cannot start with acs: or aliyun. It cannot contain http:// or https://. |

| Tag.N.Value | String | No | TestValue | The value of tag N to be bound to the key pair. Valid values of N: 1 to 20. It can be up to 128 characters in length and cannot start with acs: or contain http:// or https://. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ResourceGroupId | String | No | rg- bp67acfmxazb4p h*** | The ID of the resource group to which to assign the key pair. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| KeyPairFingerPr int | String | 89:f0:ba:62:ac:b8:a a:e1:61:5e:fd:81:69: 86:6d:6b:f0:c0:5a:** | The fingerprint of the key pair. The fingerprint uses the message-digest algorithm 5 (MD5) based on the public key fingerprint format defined in RFC 4716. For more information, see RFC 4716. |
| KeyPairId | String | ssh- bp67acfmxazb4ph** * | The ID of the key pair. |
| KeyPairName | String | TestKeyPairV23 | The name of the key pair. |
| PrivateKeyBody | String | MIIEpAIBAAKCAQEAt ReyMzLIcBH78EV2zj **** | The private key of the key pair. The private key is PEM-encoded in the PKCS#8 format. |
| RequestId | String | 473469C7-AA6F- 4DC5-B3DB- A3DC0DE3C83E | The ID of the request. |

**Examples**

```
https://ecs.example.com/?Action=CreateKeyPair &RegionId=cn-qingdao-env17-d01 &KeyPairName=TestKeyPairV23 &<Common request parameters>
```

##### 5.1.13.2 AttachKeyPair

Binds an SSH key pair to one or more Linux instances. When you call this operation, consider the following items: Windows instances do not support SSH key pairs. After an SSH key pair is attached to an ECS instance that uses password authentication, the password authentication method might be disabled. If an instance is in the Running state, you must restart the instance (RebootInstance) for the SSH key pair to take effect. If an instance is in the Stopped state, you must start the instance (StartInstance) for the SSH key pair to take effect. If an instance is already bound to an SSH key pair, the new SSH key pair will replace the original one.

**Request headers**

The AttachKeyPair operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the Common request.

**Request parameters**

| RegionId | Strin g | Quer y | Yes | cn-qingdao-env17-d01 | The region ID of the SSH key pair. You can call the DescribeRegions operation to query the most recent region list. |
| KeyPairNa me | Strin g | Quer y | Yes | KeyPairV25 | The name of the SSH key pair. |
| InstanceIds | Strin g | Quer y | Yes | ["i-xxxxxxxxx", "i- yyyyyyyyy", … "i- zzzzzzzzz"] | The IDs of instances to which you want to bind the SSH key pair. The value can be a JSON array that consists of up to 50 instance IDs. Separate multiple instance IDs with commas (,). |

| FailCount | String | 0 | The number of instances to which the SSH key pair failed to be bound. |

##### 5.1.13.3 DetachKeyPair

You can call this operation to detach an SSH key pair from one or more Linux instances. When you call this operation, take note of the following items: After you detach an SSH key pair from an instance, you must call the RebootInstance operation to restart the instance for the detach operation to take effect. By default, the username and password authentication method is used for an instance after you detach an SSH key pair from the instance.

##### 5.1.13.4 DeleteKeyPairs

You can call this operation to delete one or more SSH key pairs. After an SSH key pair is deleted: You cannot query the key pair by calling the DescribeKeyPairs operation. If the key pair was bound to one or more ECS instances: The key pair is no longer stored on Apsara Stack but the instances can still use the key pair. When you call the DescribeInstance operation to query instance information, the name of the key pair name (KeyPairNames) is still returned, but no other information about the key pair.

**Request parameters**

| RegionId | String | Yes | cn-qingdao- env17-d01 | The region ID of the key pair. You can call the DescribeRegions operation to query the most recent region list. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| RequestId | String | 473469C7-AA6F- 4DC5-B3DB- A3DC0DE3C83E | The ID of the request. |

#### 5.1.14 Elastic network interfaces

##### 5.1.14.1 CreateNetworkInterface

Creates an elastic network interface (ENI).

**Usage notes**

An ENI enters the Available (Available) state after it is created. An ENI can be attached only to a single instance of the Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) type within the same zone. An ENI can be attached only to a single instance. If you want to attach an ENI to another instance, you must detach the ENI from the current instance. When an ENI is attached to another instance, the attributes of the ENI remain unchanged and the network traffic is redirected to the new instance. If you want to assign IPv6 addresses when you create an ENI, make sure that IPv6 is enabled for the vSwitch with which you want to associate the ENI. By default, up to 100 ENIs can be created per region per Apsara Stack tenant account.

##### 5.1.14.2 AttachNetworkInterface

You can call this operation to bind an elastic network interface (ENI) to an ECS instance in a VPC. When you call this operation, take note of the following items: The ENI must be in the **Available** ( `Available` ) state. Each ENI can be bound to a single instance. The instance must be in the **Running** ( `Running` ) or **Stopped** ( `Stopped` ). When you bind ENIs to instances of some instance types, the instances must be in the **Stopped** ( `Stopped` ) state.

**Note**

If the last start time of the instance (including the last start time of the instance if it is newly purchased, the last restart time of the instance, the last reactivation time of the instance) is before April 1, 2018 and the instance stays in the Running state, you must call the RebootInstance operation to restart the instance. Otherwise, the ENI cannot be attached to the instance. You can bind multiple ENIs to a single instance. The instance must be in the same zone and the same VPC as the VSwitch to which the ENI is connected.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Require d | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | AttachNetworkInt erface | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to AttachNetworkInterface. |
| InstanceId | String | Yes | i- bp16qstyvxj9gpq w**** | The ID of the instance. |
| NetworkInterfa ceId | String | Yes | eni- bp17pdijfczax1hu ji**** | The ID of the ENI. |
| RegionId | String | Yes | cn-qingdao- env17-d01 | The region ID of the instance. You can call the DescribeRegions operation to query the most recent region list. |

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |

##### 5.1.14.3 AssignPrivateIpAddresses

Assigns one or more secondary private IP addresses to an elastic network interface (ENI). You can specify available private IP addresses within the CIDR block of the vSwitch that hosts the ENI. Alternatively, you can specify the number of private IP addresses for Elastic Compute Service (ECS) to automatically assign them. The ENI to which you want to assign private IP addresses must be in the Available (Available) or Bound (InUse) state. When you perform operations on the primary ENI, the instance to which the ENI is bound must be in the Running or Stopped state.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Require d | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| Action | String |   | Yes | AssignPrivateIpA ddresses | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to AssignPrivateIpAddresses. |   |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| NetworkInterfaceI d | String |   | Yes | eni- bp67acfmxazb4p **** | The ID of the ENI. |   |
| RegionId | String |   | Yes | cn-qingdao- env17-d01 | The region ID of the ENI. You can call the DescribeRegions operation to query the most recent region list. |   |
| PrivateIpAddress. N | RepeatLi st |   | No | 10.1.2.1 | One or more secondary private IP addresses selected from within the CIDR block of the vSwitch that hosts the ENI. Valid values of N: When the ENI is in the Available ( Available ) state, the valid values of N are 1 to 10. When the ENI is in the Bound ( InUse ) state, the valid values of N are subject to the instance type. For more information, see the Instan ce types topic in ECS Product Introdu ction. To assign secondary private IP addresses, you must specify one of the PrivateIpAddress.N and SecondaryPrivateIpAddressCount parameters but you cannot specify both of them. |   |
| SecondaryPrivate IpAddressCount | Integer |   | No | 1 | The number of private IP addresses to be automatically assigned from within the CIDR block of the vSwitch. |   |

##### 5.1.14.4 UnassignPrivateIpAddresses

You can call this operation to unassign one or more secondary private IP addresses from an elastic network interface (ENI). The ENI from which you want to unassign private IP addresses must be in the **Available** (Available) or **Bound** (InUse) state. When you perform operations on the primary ENI, the instance to which the ENI is bound must be in the **Running** (Running) or **Stopped** (Stopped) state.

##### 5.1.14.5 DescribeNetworkInterfaces

You can call this operation to query the list of elastic network interfaces (ENIs). `You can use one of the following methods to check` the responses returned by the DescribeNetworkInterfaces operation: Method 1: Use `NextToken` to configure the query token. Set the value of this parameter to the

| NextToken |   |
|---|---|
| MaxResults |   |

`NextToken` value returned in the last call to `DescribeNetworkInterfaces` . Then use `MaxResults` to set the maximum number of entries to return on each page. Method 2: Use `PageSize` to set the number of entries to return on each page and then use `PageNumber` to set the number of the page to return. You can use only one of the preceding methods. If a large number of entries are returned, we recommend that you use method 1. If `NextToken` is set, `PageSize` and `PageNumber` will not take effect and `TotalCount` in the response will be invalid.

##### 5.1.14.6 DetachNetworkInterface

You can call this operation to unbind an elastic network interface (ENI) from an ECS instance. When you call this operation, take note of the following items: The primary ENIs of ECS instances cannot be unbound. The ENI must be in the Detaching (Detaching) or Bound (InUse) state. The instance must be in the Running (Running) or Stopped (Stopped) state.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Require d | Example | Description |

| Action | String | Yes | DetachNetworkIn terface | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to DetachNetworkInterface. |

| InstanceId | String | Yes | i- bp67acfmxazb4p **** | The ID of the instance from which you want to unbind an ENI. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NetworkInterfa ceId | String | Yes | eni- bp67acfmxazb4p **** | The ID of the ENI to be unbound. |
| RegionId | String | Yes | cn-qingdao- env17-d01 | The region ID of the ENI. You can call the DescribeRegions operation to query the most recent region list. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| RequestId | String | 473469C7-AA6F- 4DC5-B3DB- A3DC0DE3C83E | The ID of the request. |

##### 5.1.14.7 DeleteNetworkInterface

You can call this operation to delete an elastic network interface (ENI). The ENI must be in the Available (Available) state. If the ENI is bound to an ECS instance, you must unbind the ENI from the ECS instance (DetachNetworkInterface) before you can delete the ENI. After an ENI is deleted: The primary private IP address of the ENI is automatically released. The ENI is automatically removed from its security groups.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Require d | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | DeleteNetworkInt erface | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to DeleteNetworkInterface. |
| NetworkInterfa ceId | String | Yes | eni- bp14v2sdd3v8htl nm*** | The ID of the ENI to be deleted. |
| RegionId | String | Yes | cn-qingdao- env17-d01 | The region ID of the ENI. You can call the DescribeRegions operation to query the most recent region list. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| RequestId | String | F3CD6886-D8D0- 4FEE-B93E- 1B73239673DE | The ID of the request. |

##### 5.1.14.9 AssignIpv6Addresses

Assigns one or more IPv6 addresses to an elastic network interface (ENI).

**Usage notes**

You can specify IPv6 addresses within the CIDR block of the vSwitch with which the ENI is associated, or specify the number of IPv6 addresses to be automatically assigned. When you call this operation, take note of the following items: The ENI must be in the **Available** ( `Available` ) or **Bound** ( `InUse` ) state. The Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance to which the primary ENI is attached must be in the
**Running** ( `Running` ) or **Stopped** ( `Stopped` ) state.
The maximum number of IPv6 addresses that can be assigned to an ENI varies based on the instance type. If the ENI is in the **Available** ( `Available` ) state, up to 10 IPv6 addresses can be assigned to the ENI. If the ENI is already attached to an ECS instance, the maximum number of IPv6 addresses that can be assigned to the ENI is determined based on the instance type. After the operation is called, you can obtain the IPv6 addresses assigned to the ENI from the response.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Require d | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| Action | String | Yes | AssignIpv6Addres ses | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to AssignIpv6Addresses. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RegionId | String | Yes | cn-qingdao-**** | The region ID of the ENI. You can call the DescribeRegions operation to query the most recent region list. |
| NetworkInterfaceI d | String | Yes | eni- bp14v2sdd3v8ht* ***** | The ENI ID. |
| Ipv6Address.N | RepeatLi st | No | 2001:db8:1234:1 a00::**** | IPv6 address N to assign to the ENI. Valid values of N: 1 to 10. Example: Ipv6Address.1=2001:db8:1234:1a00:: XXX Note You must specify Ipv6Addresses.N or Ipv6AddressCount but not both. |
| Ipv6AddressCoun t | Integer | No | 1 | The number of IPv6 addresses to generate at random for the ENI. Valid values: 1 to 10. Note You must specify Ipv6Addresses.N or Ipv6AddressCount but not both. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ipv6Sets | List | 2001:db8:1234:1a0 0::**** | The IPv6 addresses assigned to the ENI. |
| NetworkInterfa ceId | String | eni- bp1iqejowblx6h8j*** * | The ENI ID. |
| RequestId | String | 473469C7-AA6F- 4DC5-B3DB- A3DC0DE***** | The request ID. |

#### 5.1.15 System events

##### 5.1.15.1 DescribeInstanceHistoryEvents

Queries the system events of Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances. By default, system events that are in the Executed, Avoided, Canceled, or Failed state can be queried by calling the DescribeInstanceHistoryEvents operation. You can specify InstanceEventCycleStatus.N to query system events in a specific state.

**Usage notes**

You can query system events that were completed within the last 30 days. No limits apply to the time range for querying uncompleted system events. You can also specify `InstanceEventCycleStatus` to query the system events that are in the Scheduled, Executing, or Inquiring state.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Require d | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | DescribeInstance HistoryEvents | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to DescribeInstanceHistoryEvents. |
| RegionId | String | Yes | cn-qingdao-***** | The region ID of the instance. You can call the DescribeRegions operation to query the most recent region list. |
| InstanceId | String | No | i- uf678mass4zvr9n 1**** | The ID of the instance. If this parameter is not specified, the system events of all instances in the specified region are queried. |

| EventId.N | RepeatLi st | No | e- uf64yvznlao4jl2c **** | The ID of system event N. Valid values of N: 1 to 100. Specify multiple event IDs in the repeated list form. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| InstanceEventCyc leStatus.N | RepeatLi st | No | Executed | The lifecycle state of system event N. Valid values of N: 1 to 7. Specify multiple states in the repeated list form. Valid values: Scheduled Avoided Executing Executed Canceled Failed Inquiring |
| EventCycleStatus | String | No | Executed | The lifecycle state of the system event. EventCycleStatus is valid only when InstanceEventCycleStatus.N is not specified. Valid values: Scheduled Avoided Executing Executed Canceled Failed Inquiring |
| InstanceEventTyp e.N | RepeatLi st | No | SystemMaintena nce.Reboot | The type of system event N. Valid values of N: 1 to 30. Specify multiple types in the repeated list form. Valid values: SystemMaintenance.Reboot: The instance is restarted due to system maintenance. SystemMaintenance.Redeploy: The instance is redeployed due to system maintenance. SystemFailure.Reboot: The instance is restarted due to a system error. SystemFailure.Redeploy: The instance is redeployed due to a system error. SystemFailure.Delete: The instance is released due to an instance creation failure. InstanceFailure.Reboot: The instance is restarted due to an instance error. |

| EventType | String | No | SystemMaintena nce.Reboot | The type of the system event. EventType is valid only when InstanceEventType.N is not specified. Valid values: SystemMaintenance.Reboot: The instance is restarted due to system maintenance. SystemMaintenance.Redeploy: The instance is redeployed due to system maintenance. SystemFailure.Reboot: The instance is restarted due to a system error. SystemFailure.Redeploy: The instance is redeployed due to a system error. SystemFailure.Delete: The instance is released due to an instance creation failure. InstanceFailure.Reboot: The instance is restarted due to an instance error. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NotBefore.Start | String | No | 2017-11- 30T06:32:31Z | The start time of the scheduled execution of the system event. Specify the time in the ISO 8601 standard in the yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ format. The time must be in UTC. |
| NotBefore.End | String | No | 2017-12- 01T06:32:31Z | The end time of the scheduled execution of the system event. Specify the time in the ISO 8601 standard in the yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ format. The time must be in UTC. |
| EventPublishTime .Start | String | No | 2017-11- 30T06:32:31Z | The beginning of the time range in which to query published system events. Specify the time in the ISO 8601 standard in the yyyy-MM- ddTHH:mm:ssZ format. The time must be in UTC. |
| EventPublishTime .End | String | No | 2017-12- 01T06:32:31Z | The end of the time range in which to query published system events. Specify the time in the ISO 8601 standard in the yyyy-MM- ddTHH:mm:ssZ format. The time must be in UTC. |
| ImpactLevel | String | No | 100 | The impact level of the system event. |
| PageNumber | Integer | No | 1 | The page number. Pages start from page 1. The value must be a positive integer. Default value: 1. |

##### 5.1.16.3 DescribeAvailableResource

Queries resources in a specific zone. You can query the resources available in a zone before you create Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances by calling the RunInstances operation or before you modify instance types by calling the ModifyInstanceSpec operation. Usage notes The value of `DestinationResource` determines whether you need to specify additional parameters. When you select a value in the following chain for DestinationResource, the more to the right the selected value is ordered, the more parameters you must specify. `Sequence:` Zone > IoOptimized > InstanceType = Network = ddh > SystemDisk > DataDisk Examples: If you set `DestinationResource` to `DataDisk` , you must specify `InstanceType` or set `ResourceType` to `disk` . If you set `DestinationResource` to `SystemDisk` , you must specify `InstanceType` .

**Request headers**

This operation uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request headers" topic.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Positi on | Required | Example | Description |

| RegionId | Strin g | Quer y | Yes | cn-qingdao-env17-**** | The region ID. You can call the DescribeRegions operation to query the most recent region list. |
| InstanceCh argeType | Strin g | Quer y | No |   | This parameter is not supported. |
| SpotStrateg y | Strin g | Quer y | No |   | This parameter is not supported. |
| SpotDurati on | Integ er | Quer y | No |   | This parameter is not supported. |

| Destination Resource | Strin g | Quer y | Yes | InstanceType | The resource type. Valid values: Zone: zone IoOptimized: I/O optimized resource InstanceType: instance type SystemDisk: system disk DataDisk: data disk Network: network type ddh: dedicated host For more information about how to set the DestinationResource parameter, see the "Usage notes" section in this topic. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ZoneId | Strin g | Quer y | No | cn-qingdao-env17-*****-a | The zone ID. This parameter is empty by default. When this parameter is empty, the system returns resources that match the other criteria in all zones within the region specified by RegionId . |
| IoOptimize d | Strin g | Quer y | No | optimized | Specifies whether the instance is I/O optimized. Valid values: none: a non-I/O optimized instance optimized: an I/O optimized instance Default value: optimized. |

You can also call the DescribeInstanceTypes operation to obtain the latest instance types. For more information about how to set the InstanceType parameter, see the "Usage notes" section in this topic. |

Valid values: cloud efficiency: ultra _ disk cloud ssd: standard SSD _ cloud pperf: premium _ performance disk cloud sperf: standard _ performance disk san ssd: shared SSD _ san efficiency: shared _ ultra disk Default value: cloud efficiency. _ By default, shared standard SSDs and shared ultra disks cannot be created. |

##### 5.1.16.4 DescribeResourcesModification

You can call this operation to query available resources in a zone when you upgrade or downgrade instance types or replace system disks.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Require d | Example | Description |

| Action | String | Yes | DescribeResourc esModification | The operation that you want to perform. If you use a custom HTTP URL or HTTPS URL to make an API request, you must specify the Action parameter. Set the value to DescribeResourcesModification. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DestinationRes ource | String | Yes | InstanceType | The type of the resource. Valid values: InstanceType SystemDisk |
| RegionId | String | Yes | cn-qingdao- env17-d01 | The ID of the region. You can call the DescribeRegions operation to query the most recent region list. |
| ResourceId | String | Yes | i- bp67acfmxazb4p **** | The ID of the resource. For example, when DestinationResource is set to InstanceType, this parameter can be interpreted as InstanceId. |
| MigrateAcrossZ one | Boolean | No | true | Specifies whether to allow cross- cluster instance type upgrades. Valid values: true false Default value: false |

#### 5.1.17 Operations and monitoring

##### 5.1.17.1 GetInstanceConsoleOutput

You can call this operation to obtain the command output of an instance. The returned command output is encoded in Base64. ECS is a virtualized cloud-based service and cannot be connected to display devices. However, the command output for the last start, restart, or shutdown of each instance is cached. ##### 5.1.17.2 GetInstanceScreenshot

You can call this operation to obtain screenshots of an instance. ECS returns an instance screenshot that is in the JPG format and encoded in Base64. You must decode the screenshot. We recommend that you call this operation for troubleshooting and diagnosis. When you call this operation, take note of the following items: The instance must be in the Running state. If you call this operation on the same instance for multiple times, the call interval must be at least 10 seconds. Otherwise, the `Throttling` error code is returned.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Require d | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | GetInstanceScree nshot | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to GetInstanceScreenshot. |
| InstanceId | String | Yes | i- bp1gbz20g229bv u5**** | The ID of the instance. |
| RegionId | String | Yes | cn-qingdao- env17-d01 | The region ID of the instance. You can call the DescribeRegions operation to query the most recent region list. |
| WakeUp | Boolean | No | false | Specifies whether to wake up the instance that is in sleep mode. Default value: false |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| InstanceId | String | i- bp1gbz20g229bvu5 **** | The ID of the instance. |

| RequestId | String | 473469C7-AA6F- 4DC5-B3DB- A3DC0DE3C83E | The ID of the request. |
|---|---|---|---|
| Screenshot | String | iVBORw0KGgoA...AA ABJRU5ErkJggg== | The JPG-formatted instance screenshot, which is encoded in Base64. |

##### 5.1.17.3 DescribeSnapshotMonitorData

You can call this operation to query all monitoring data about snapshot size changes in a region over the past 30 days. When you call this operation, take note of the following items: Up to 400 monitoring data entries can be returned at a time. An error is returned if the value

| (EndTime − StartTime)/Period |   |   |
|---|---|---|
| . If the value of | StartTime | is |

calculated based on the following formula is greater than 400: (EndTime − StartTime)/Period . You can query the monitoring data from up to the past 30 days. If the value of `StartTime` is more than 30 days earlier than the current time, an error is returned.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Require d | Example | Description |

| Action | String | Yes | DescribeSnapsho tMonitorData | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to DescribeSnapshotMonitorData. |

| RegionId | String | Yes | cn-qingdao- env17-d01 | The ID of the region. You can call the DescribeRegions operation to query the most recent region list. |
| StartTime | String | Yes | 2019-05- 10T00:00:00Z | The beginning of the time range to query. Specify the time in the ISO 8601 standard in the yyyy-MM- ddTHH:mm:ssZ format. The time must be in UTC. If the value of seconds (ss) is not 00, the time is rounded up to the next minute. |
| Period | Integer | No | 60 | The interval at which to retrieve snapshot size changes. Unit: seconds. Valid values: 60 600 3600 Default value: 60 |

| Category | String | No | Standard | The type of the snapshot. Valid values: Standard: normal snapshot Flash: local snapshot Default value: Standard |
|---|---|---|---|---|

##### 5.1.17.4 DescribeEniMonitorData

You can call this operation to query all monitoring data about traffic on a secondary elastic network interface (ENI) over a specific period of time. The monitoring data includes traffic sent and received over the internal network, the number of packets sent and received by the secondary ENI, and the number of dropped packets sent and received by the secondary ENI. A portion may be missing from the returned monitoring data. This is because the system cannot obtain the relevant information. For example, if the instance to which the secondary ENI is bound is in the Stopped state, or if the secondary ENI is not bound to an instance and in the Available state, monitoring data about traffic on the ENI cannot be obtained. When you call this operation, take note of the following items: Up to 400 monitoring data entries can be returned at a time. An error is returned if the value calculated based on the following formula is greater than 400: (EndTime − StartTime)/Period. You can query monitoring data from up to the past 30 days. If the value of StartTime is more than 30 days earlier than the current time, an error is returned.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Require d | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | DescribeEniMonit orData | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to DescribeEniMonitorData. |
| EndTime | String | Yes | 2018-05- 21T12:22:00Z | The end of the time range to query. Specify the time in the ISO 8601 standard in the yyyy-MM- ddTHH:mm:ssZ format. The time must be in UTC. If the value of seconds (ss) is not 00, the time is rounded up to the next minute. |
| InstanceId | String | Yes | i- m5e88p52tbip9r 2x**** | The ID of the instance to which the secondary ENI is bound. |

| RegionId | String | Yes | cn-qingdao- env17-d01 | The region ID of the secondary ENI. You can call the DescribeRegions operation to query the most recent region list. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| StartTime | String | Yes | 2018-05- 21T12:19:00Z | The beginning of the time range to query. Specify the time in the ISO 8601 standard in the yyyy-MM- ddTHH:mm:ssZ format. The time must be in UTC. If the value of seconds (ss) is not 00, the time is rounded up to the next minute. |
| EniId | String | No | eni- m5e0ajic0vbwx7l 3**** | The ID of the secondary ENI. By default, all secondary ENIs that are bound to the specified instance are queried. |
| Period | Integer | No | 60 | The interval at which to retrieve monitoring data. Unit: seconds. Valid values: 60 600 3600 Default value: 60 |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| MonitorData | Array |   | The collection of monitoring data about traffic on the secondary ENI. |
| EniMonitorData |   |   |   |
| DropPacketRx | String | 0 | The number of inbound internal data packets discarded by the secondary ENI. |
| DropPacketTx | String | 0 | The number of outbound internal data packets discarded by the secondary ENI. |
| EniId | String | eni- m5e0ajic0vbwx7l3* *** | The ID of the secondary ENI. |
| IntranetRx | String | 0 | The internal data traffic received by the secondary ENI. Unit: Kbit/s. |
| IntranetTx | String | 0 | The internal data traffic sent by the secondary ENI. Unit: Kbit/s. |

| PacketRx | String | 0 | The number of internal data packets received by the secondary ENI. Unit: packets. |

#### 5.1.18 Cloud Assistant

##### 5.1.18.1 CreateCommand

Creates a Cloud Assistant command.

**Usage notes**

You can create commands of the following types: Batch commands (RunBatScript), applicable to Windows instances PowerShell commands (RunPowerShellScript), applicable to Windows instances Shell commands (RunShellScript), applicable to Linux instances You can specify TimeOut to set the maximum timeout period for executions of a command on Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances. If an execution times out, Cloud Assistant Agent forcefully terminates the command process by canceling the process ID (PID) of the command. For a one-time task, when the execution times out, the state of the command (InvokeRecordStatus) becomes Failed. For a scheduled task, take note of the following items: The timeout period takes effect on each execution. When an execution times out, the state (InvokeRecordStatus) of the command becomes Failed. The timeout of one execution does not affect the subsequent executions. You can use WorkingDir to specify the working directory of a Cloud Assistant command. For Linux instances, the default working directory of Cloud Assistant commands is the home directory of the root user, which is `/root` . For Windows instances, the default working directory of Cloud Assistant commands is the directory where the Cloud Assistant Agent process resides, such as C:\Windows\System32. You can enable the custom parameter feature for a Cloud Assistant command by setting EnableParameter to true when you create the command. When you specify CommandContent, you can define custom parameters in the {{parameter}} format. Then, when the InvokeCommand operation is called, the key-value pairs of custom parameters are passed in. For example, if a command is `echo {{name}}` , the Parameters parameter can be used to pass in the `<name, Jack>` key-value pair when the InvokeCommand operation is called. The name key of the custom parameter is automatically replaced by the paired Jack value to generate a new command. As a result, the `echo Jack` command is actually run.

**Request parameters**

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | CreateCommand | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to CreateCommand. |
| CommandConten t | String | Yes | ZWNobyAxMjM= | The Base64-encoded content of the command. The value must be Base64-encoded and cannot exceed 18 KB in size. Custom parameters can be added to the command. To enable the custom parameter feature, set EnableParameter to true. Custom parameters are defined in the {{}} format. Within {{}} , the spaces and line feeds before and after the parameter names are ignored. You can specify up to 20 custom parameters. A custom parameter name can contain only letters , digits , underscores ( ) , _ and hyphens (-) . The name is case-insensitive. Each custom parameter name cannot exceed 64 bytes in length. |
| Name | String | Yes | testName | The name of the command. The name supports all character sets and can be up to 128 characters in length. |

|   | {{}} |

RunPowerShellScript: PowerShell command. PowerShell commands are applicable to Windows instances. RunShellScript: shell command. Shell commands are applicable to Linux instances. |

##### 5.1.18.2 InvokeCommand

Triggers a Cloud Assistant command on Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances.

**Usage notes**

ECS instances on which to run the Cloud Assistant command must meet the following requirements. If you specify multiple ECS instances and one of the instances does not meet the requirements for running the command, the call fails. Specify instances that meet the requirements and call the InvokeCommand operation again. The ECS instances resides within virtual private clouds (VPCs). The instances are in the Running ( `Running` ) state. Cloud Assistant Agent is installed on the instances. For information about how to install Cloud Assistant Agent, see InstallCloudAssistant. Before you run PowerShell commands, make sure that the PowerShell module is configured for the instances. If you set `Timed` to false, the command is run only once. If you set `Timed` to true, the command is run on a schedule. The schedule is specified by the `Frequency` parameter. The results of each execution of a command do not affect the next execution of the command. The schedule on which the command is run on an ECS instance must be specified based on the system time of the instance in UTC. Make sure that the time or time zone of the instance meets your business requirements. Command executions may fail due to instance status exceptions, network exceptions, or exceptions on Cloud Assistant Agent. If an execution fails, no execution information is generated. If you enable the custom parameter feature by setting EnableParameter to true when you create a command, you must specify custom parameters ( `Parameters` ) when you run the command.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Require d | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | InvokeCommand | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to InvokeCommand. |
| CommandId | String | Yes | c- e9962872063249 75b5fbe1d******* * | The command ID. You can call the DescribeCommands operation to query all available command IDs. |
| InstanceId.N | RepeatLi st | Yes | i- bp185dy2o3o6n* ***** | The ID of instance N on which to run the command. You can specify up to 50 instance IDs in each request. Valid values of N: 1 to 50. |
| RegionId | String | Yes | cn-qingdao-**** | The region ID of the command. You can call the DescribeRegions operation to query the most recent region list. |

| RepeatMode | String | No | Once | Specifies how to run the command. Valid values: Once: immediately runs the command. Period: runs the command on a schedule. If you set this parameter to Period , you must set Timed to true and specify Frequency . NextRebootOnly: automatically runs the command the next time the instance is started. EveryReboot: automatically runs the command every time the instance is started. Default value: If you set Timed to false and do not specify Frequency , the default value of RepeatMode is Once . If you set Timed to true and specify Frequency , Period is used as the value of RepeatMode regardless of whether you specify RepeatMode. Note: If you set this parameter to Period , NextRebootOnly , or EveryReboot , you can call the StopInvocation operation to stop the pending or scheduled execution of the command. If you set this parameter to Period or EveryReboot , you can call the DescribeInvocationResults operation and set IncludeHistory to true to view the results of previous scheduled executions. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Timed | Boolean | No | true | Specifies whether to run the command on a schedule. Valid values: true false Default value: false. |

| Frequency | String | No | 0 */20 * * * * | The schedule on which to run the command. The interval at which the command is run on a schedule must be at least 10 seconds. When you set Timed to true , you must specify Frequency . The value of Frequency is a cron expression. For more information, see the "Cron expression" topic in ECS User Guide. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Parameters | Json | No | {"name":"Jack", "accessKey":"LTA Idyv******aRY"} | The key-value pairs of custom parameters to pass in when the custom parameter feature is enabled. Number of custom parameters: 0 to 10. Each key in a Map collection cannot be an empty string and can be up to 64 characters in length. Values in a Map collection can be empty strings. The size of the command after Base64 encoding, including the custom parameters and the original command content, cannot exceed 18 KB. The custom parameter names that are specified by the Parameters parameter must be included in the custom parameter names that you specified when you created the command. You can use empty strings to represent the parameters that are not passed in. If you want to disable the custom parameter feature, you can leave this parameter empty. |
| Username | String | No | root | The username to use to run the command on ECS instances. Note The parameter is valid only when the command is run on Linux instances. For Linux instances, the default username is root. |

##### 5.1.18.3 RunCommand

Runs a shell, PowerShell, or batch command on Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances.

**Usage notes**

Unlike the CreateCommand and InvokeCommand operations, RunCommand can be used to create and run a command in a single request. Take note of the following items: The instances on which you want to run a command must reside in a virtual private cloud (VPC). The instances must be in the Running ( `Running` ) state. The Cloud Assistant client must be installed on the instances. For more information, see InstallCloudAssistant. Before you run a PowerShell command on a Windows instance, make sure that the PowerShell module is installed on the instance. The schedule on which to run a command on an ECS instance must be specified based on the system time of the instance in UTC. Make sure that the time or time zone of the ECS instance meets your business needs. You can specify `TimeOut` to set the timeout period of command executions on instances. When an execution times out, the command process is forcefully terminated. After a one-time execution times out, the execution state (InvokeRecordStatus) of the command becomes Failed. For recurring executions, the timeout period takes effect on each execution. The timeout of each execution does not affect the next execution. After an execution times out, the execution state (InvokeRecordStatus) of the command becomes Failed. Commands that are run may fail due to instance status exceptions, network exceptions, or exceptions on the Cloud Assistant client. If a command fails to be run, no execution information is generated. When `EnableParameter` is set to true, the custom parameter feature is enabled. When you specify `CommandContent` , you can specify custom parameters in the `{{parameter}}` format. Then, when the command is run, the key-value pairs of the custom parameters are passed in.

**Request parameters**

Take note of the following items: If you want to retain the command, make sure that the Base64-encoded command content does not exceed 18 KB in size. If you do not want to retain the command, make sure that the Base64-encoded command content does not exceed 24 KB in size. You can set KeepCommand to specify whether to retain the command. If the command content is Base64- encoded, set ContentEncoding to Base64. When EnableParameter is set to true, the custom parameter feature is enabled and you can configure custom parameters based on the following rules: Define custom parameters in the {{}} format. Within {{}} , the spaces and line feeds before and after the parameter names are ignored. You can specify up to 20 custom parameters. ##### 5.1.18.5 ModifyCommand

Modifies the parameters and content of a Cloud Assistant command.

**Usage notes**

You can modify a command when it is run. After the command is modified, the new command applies to subsequent executions. The command type cannot be changed. For example, a shell command (RunShellScript) cannot be changed to a batch command (RunBatScript).

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Require d | Example | Description |

| RegionId | String | Yes | cn-qingdao-***** | The region ID of the command. You can call the DescribeRegions operation to query the most recent region list. |
| Name | String | No | AlibabaCommand | The name of the command. The name supports all character sets and can be up to 128 characters in length. |
| Description | String | No | UserGuide | The description of the command. The description supports all character sets and can be up to 512 characters in length. |

| CommandConten t | String | No | c2VydmljZSB0b2 1jYXQgc3RhcnQ= | The content of the command. The command content can be plaintext or Base64-encoded. Take note of the following items: The Base64-encoded command content cannot exceed 16 KB in size. If the command content is Base64- encoded, set ContentEncoding to Base64. When EnableParameter is set to true, the custom parameter feature is enabled and you can configure custom parameters based on the following rules: Define custom parameters in the {{}} format. Within {{}} , the spaces and line feeds before and after the parameter names are ignored. You can specify up to 20 custom parameters. A custom parameter name can contain only letters , digits , underscores ( ) , _ and hyphens (-) . The name is case-insensitive. Each custom parameter name cannot exceed 64 bytes in length. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| WorkingDir | String | No | /home/ | The working directory of the command. |
| Timeout | Long | No | 60 | The maximum timeout period for the command execution. Unit: seconds. When a command cannot run within the specified period of time, a timeout error occurs. When a command execution times out, the Cloud Assistant client force-stops the command process by canceling the PID of the command. |

##### 5.1.18.6 StopInvocation

Stops the process of a Cloud Assistant command that is running on one or more Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances. If you stop the process of a command that runs only once, the executions that have started are not interrupted. The executions that have not started are canceled. If you stop the process of a command that runs on a recurring schedule, the executions that have started are not interrupted but subsequent executions are cancelled.

##### 5.1.18.8 DescribeInvocations

Queries the list of tasks and execution status of Cloud Assistant commands. After you run a command, the command may not succeed or return the expected results. You can call this operation to query the actual execution results. You can query the execution information that is generated within the last two weeks. Up to 100,000 lines of execution information can be retained.

##### 5.1.18.9 DescribeCloudAssistantStatus

Queries whether the Cloud Assistant client is installed on one or more Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances. If the Cloud Assistant client is installed, the system queries the total number of Cloud Assistant commands that have been run, the number of Cloud Assistant commands that are being run, and the time when Cloud Assistant commands were last run.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Require d | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | DescribeCloudAs sistantStatus | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to DescribeCloudAssistantStatus. |
| RegionId | String | Yes | cn-qingdao-**** | The region ID of the ECS instance. You can call the DescribeRegions operation to query the most recent region list. |
| OSType | String | No | Windows | The operating system type of the instance. Valid values: Windows Linux |
| PageNumber | Long | No | 1 | The page number. Pages start from page 1. Default value: 1. |

| PageSize | Long | No | 10 | The number of entries per page. Valid values: 1 to 100. Default value: 10. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| InstanceId.N | RepeatLi st | No | i- bp1iudwa5b1tqa* ***** | The ID of instance N. The ID of instance N. You can specify up to 50 instance IDs in each request. Valid values of N: 1 to 50. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| InstanceCloudA ssistantStatusS et | Array of InstanceCloudA ssistantStatus |   | Details about the installation status of the Cloud Assistant client on the instances. |
| InstanceCloudA ssistantStatus |   |   |   |
| ActiveTaskCou nt | Long | 1 | The number of commands that are being run. |

##### 5.1.18.11 SendFile

Sends a file to one or more Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances.

**Usage notes**

The instances to which you want to send a file must be in the Running ( `Running` ) state. The Cloud Assistant client must be installed on the instances. The file that you want to send must not exceed 32 KB in size after it is encoded in Base64. The file may fail to be sent due to instance exceptions, network exceptions, or exceptions on the Cloud Assistance client. Call the DescribeSendFileResults operation to troubleshoot the issues.

**Request parameters**

The content must not exceed 32 KB in size after it is encoded in Base64. If ContentType is set to PlainText , the value of Content is in plaintext. If ContentType is set to Base64 , the value of Content is Base64-encoded. |
| InstanceId.N | RepeatLi st | Yes | i- bp185dy2o3o6n* *** | The ID of instance N to which you want to send the file. Up to 50 instance IDs can be specified in each request. Valid values of N: 1 to 50. |
| Name | String | Yes | file.txt | The name of the file. The name supports all character sets and can be up to 255 characters in length. |
| RegionId | String | Yes | cn-qingdao-**** | The region ID of the instance. You can call the DescribeRegions operation to query the most recent region list. |

|---|---|
| PlainText |   |

|   | ContentType |
|---|---|

##### 5.1.18.12 DescribeSendFileResults

Queries the files sent by Cloud Assistant and their states.

**Usage notes**

When you send a file, the file may fail to be sent to specified Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances. You must call this operation to check the file sending results. You can call this operation to query the file sending records of the last two weeks. A maximum of 100,000 file sending records can be retained.

| PageSize | Long | No | 10 | The number of entries per page. Valid values: 1 to 50. Default value: 10. |

|---|---|---|---|

Valid values: Pending: The system is verifying or sending the file. If the sending state of the file on at least one instance is Pending, the overall sending state of the file is Pending. Running: The file creation task is running on the instances. If the sending state of the file on at least one instance is Running, the overall sending state of the file is Running. Success: If the sending state of the file on all the instances is Success, the overall sending state of the file is Success. Failed: If the sending state of the file on all the instances is Failed, the overall sending state of the file is Failed. If the sending state of the file on one or more instances is one of the following values, the overall sending state of the file is Failed: Invalid: The file is invalid. Aborted: The file failed to be sent. Failed: The file failed to be created. Timeout: The file sending task timed out. Error: An error occurred while the file was being sent. PartialFailed: The file was sent to some of the specified instances and failed to be sent to other instances. ##### 5.1.19.3 DescribeTags

You can call this operation to query available tags. You can query tags by specifying filter conditions such as resource type, resource ID, tag key, and tag value. The specified filter conditions have logical AND relations. Only the tags that meet all the specified filter conditions are returned. If a tag key is specified and no tag values are specified, all tags that contain the tag key are returned. If a tag key-value pair is specified, only tags that exactly match the key-value pair are returned.

##### 5.1.19.5 ListTagResources

Queries the tags that are added to one or more Elastic Compute Service (ECS) resources and these ECS resources. You must specify at least one of the following parameters or parameter pairs in the request to determine a query object: the `ResourceId.N` parameter, the `Tag.N` parameter pair ( `Tag.N.Key` and `Tag.N.Value` ), and the `TagFilter.N` parameter pair (TagFilter.N.TagKey and TagFilter.N.TagValues.N). If one of the following sets of request parameters is specified as filter conditions, the response contains only ECS resources that meet all these filter conditions: Set 1: `Tag.N.Key, Tag.N.Value` , and `ResourceId.N` Set 2: `TagFilter.N.TagKey and TagFilter.N.TagValues.N` , and `ResourceId.N`

Valid values: instance: ECS instance disk: Elastic Block Storage device snapshot: snapshot image: image securitygroup: security group volume: storage volume eni: elastic network interface (ENI) ddh: dedicated host keypair: SSH key pair |
|   |   |   |   | The key of tag N used for fuzzy search of ECS resources. The tag key must be 1 to 128 characters in length. Valid values of N: 1 to 5. |

In the specified tags, a single tag key may correspond to one or more tag values. Fuzzy search may have a latency of 2 seconds. A fuzzy search can return a result set of up to 5,000 resources. When you use TagFilter.N.TagKey for fuzzy search of ECS resources, you must leave TagFilter.N.TagValues.N empty. For example, to query ECS resources that have the tag with the environment tag key added, you can set TagFilter.1.TagKey to env , but you must leave TagFilter.1.TagValues empty.
