#### 5.1.21 Appendix

##### 5.1.21.1 Terms

This topic describes the terms that may be used in ECS API operations. The following table describes the terms that may be used in ECS API operations.

| Term | Full name | Description |
|---|---|---|
| instance | Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance | An ECS instance is a virtual computer that uses the computing resources available in a physical machine. |
| region |   | A region is a separate geographic area where resources reside. Each region consists of one or more zones. |

| zone | zone | A physical area with an independent network and power supply. A region can be divided into multiple zones. Network latency is short for communication between ECS instances in the same zone. Zones in each region are connected over the internal network. When a zone becomes unavailable, the other zones are not affected. |
|---|---|---|
| image | image file | An image file can be built based on the data of an operating system and applications. You can select an image to initialize an ECS instance. An image contains all data necessary to create an ECS instance. The system disk of a new instance is a complete copy of the image that is used to create the instance, and contains the operating system and software configurations from the image. To create instances of different operating systems, you must select different image files. |
| disk |   | A disk is a storage device used by an instance. |
| snapshot |   | A snapshot is a copy of data on a disk for a specific point in time. A snapshot can be used to restore disk data and create custom images. |
| IP | IP address | A public IP address. |
| security group | security group | A security group acts as a virtual firewall to control traffic to or from ECS instances. Each ECS instance must belong to at least one security group. You can create security group rules in security groups. The security group rules of a security group apply to all instances in the security group. |
| CIDR | Classless Inter- Domain Routing | CIDR is a new addressing scheme for the Internet and allows for more efficient allocation of IP addresses than the old Class A, B, and C addressing schemes. For example, to convert the IP address segment 10.203.96.0 to 10.203.127.255 into a CIDR block, find the same first 19 bits. 10.203.0110 0000.0000 0000 to 10.203.0111 1111.1111 1111 can be represented by 10.203.96.0/19. |

**Limits**

ECS enforces quotas on the number of instances, security groups, and other resources that can be used by each user. Limits apply to instance types, the number of disks per instance, disk capacity, and the number of disk snapshots.

##### 5.1.21.5 How to ensure idempotency

If a request timeout or internal server error occurs when you call CreateInstance to create an ECS instance, the client may attempt to resend the request. You can specify the **ClientToken** parameter to prevent the server from creating redundant instances in these cases. The
**ClientToken** parameter ensures idempotency of the request.
A **ClientToken** is a unique and case-sensitive string generated by the client. It cannot exceed 64 ASCII characters in length. If you use the same **ClientToken** for multiple CreateInstance operations, the server will return identical responses that contain the same **InstanceId** parameter. Therefore, if an error occurs during an instance creation request, you can retry the creation request using the same
**ClientToken** as the failed request. This ensures that only one ECS instance is created and that it
assigned to a specific **InstanceId**. If you specify a **ClientToken** that is in use with different request parameters than previously used, ECS will return the **IdempotentParameterMismatch** error code. You must change the
**SignatureNonce**, **Timestamp**, and **Signature** values when calling the operation again. This is
because ECS uses **SignatureNonce** to prevent replay attacks and **Timestamp** to mark the time of each request. Each new request must have different **SignatureNonce** and **Timestamp** values, which changes the **Signature** value. Typically, if a 500 (InternalError) or 503 (ServiceUnavailable) error code is returned or no responses are returned, you must retry operations. If an operation is retried after a response code of 200 is returned, an identical response will be returned but the server status will not be affected. If a 4xx error code is returned and try it later does not appear in the error message, attempts to retry the operation will fail.

##### 5.1.21.6 API behavior when an instance is locked for security reasons

**security reasons**

When OperationLocks in the DescribeInstances response contains LockReason: security for an instance, the instance is locked for security reasons. If a disk on the instance is in the In_use state, the behavior of API operations related to the disk is subject to the OperationLocks settings of the instance. If the disk is in other states, the OperationLocks settings can be ignored. Table 1. Operations and behavior

| Operation | Behavior |
|---|---|
| AttachDisk | Returns an error. |
| AuthorizeSecurityGroup | Is called and returns a response based on its normal logic. |
| CreateDisk | Is called and returns a response based on its normal logic. |
| CreateImage | Is called and returns a response based on its normal logic. |
| CreateInstance | - |
| CreateSecurityGroup | Is called and returns a response based on its normal logic. |
| CreateSnapshot | Returns an error when the disk is attached to the current instance and is in the In use state. _ |
| DeleteDisk | Is called and returns a response based on its normal logic. |
| DeleteImage | Is called and returns a response based on its normal logic. |
| DeleteInstance | Is called and returns a response based on its normal logic. |
| DeleteSecurityGroup | Is called and returns a response based on its normal logic. |
| DeleteSnapshot | Is called and returns a response based on its normal logic. |
| DescribeAutoSnapshotPolicy | Is called and returns a response based on its normal logic. |

##### 5.1.21.7 ISO 8601 date and time formats

ISO 8601 Data elements and interchange formats – Information interchange – Representation of dates and times is an international standard covering the exchange of date- and time-related data. It was issued by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO). ECS open APIs adopt the ISO 8601 standard date and time formats.

## 6 Appendixes

### 6.1 STS overview

#### 6.1.1 What is STS?

Apsara Stack Security Token Service (STS) allows you to manage temporary credentials to your Apsara Stack resources. Resource Access Management (RAM) provides RAM users and roles. A RAM role does not have permanent identity credentials. A RAM role can be assumed for Apsara Stack resource access only by using an STS token. When an STS token is issued, you can specify a validity period and access permissions for the STS token.

**Use an STS token to assume a RAM role**

An authorized RAM user can use an AccessKey pair to call the AssumeRole operation. This way, the RAM user can obtain an STS token of a RAM role and use the STS token to access Apsara Stack resources.

**Benefits**

STS tokens reduce the risks of AccessKey pair leaks. An AccessKey pair is a long-term credential for a RAM user. STS tokens are temporary credentials. You can specify a validity period for an STS token. The token automatically becomes invalid when it expires. You do not need to rotate STS tokens on a regular basis. You can attach custom policies to STS tokens for flexible and fine-grained authorization.

#### 6.1.2 Obtain an STS token

You can call the AssumeRole operation to obtain a Security Token Service (STS) token. A Resource Access Management (RAM) user can use the STS token to assume a RAM role whose trusted entity is an Alibaba Cloud account.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Requir ed | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | Obtain an STS token | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to AssumeRole. |
| RoleArn | String | Yes | acs:ram::1234567 89012****:role/ad minrole | The Alibaba Cloud Resource Name (ARN) of the RAM role. The trusted entity of the RAM role is an Alibaba Cloud account. |

| RoleSessionNam e | String | Yes | alice | The custom name of the role session. Set this parameter based on your business requirements. In most cases, you can set this parameter to the identity of the API caller. For example, you can specify a username. You can specify RoleSessionName to identify API callers that assume the same RAM role in ActionTrail logs. This allows you to track the users that perform the operations. The value must be 2 to 64 characters in length, and can contain letters, digits, periods (.), at signs (@), hyphens (-), and underscores ( ). _ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Policy | String | No | {"Statement": [{"Action": ["*"],"Effect": "Allow","Resource ": ["*"]}],"Version":" 1"} | The policy that specifies the permissions of the returned STS token. You can use this parameter to grant the STS token fewer permissions than the permissions granted to the RAM role. Details: If you specify this parameter, the permissions of the returned STS token are the permissions that are included in the value of this parameter and owned by the RAM role. If you do not specify this parameter, the returned STS token has all the permissions of the RAM role. The value of the parameter must be 1 to 1,024 characters in length. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| RequestId | String | 6894B13B-6D71- 4EF5-88FA- F32781734A7F | The request ID. |
| Credentials | N/A | None | The STS credentials. |
| AccessKeyId | String | STS.L4aBSCSJVMuKg 5U1**** | The AccessKey ID. |
| AccessKeySecret | String | ****************************************** | The AccessKey secret. |
| SecurityToken | String | ******** | The STS token. |

| Expiration | String | 2015-04- 09T11:52:19Z | The time when the STS token expires. |
|---|---|---|---|
| AssumedRoleUser | N/A | None | The temporary identity that you use to assume the RAM role. |
| Arn | String | acs:ram::123456789 012****:role/adminro le/alice | The ARN of the temporary identity that you use to assume the RAM role. |
| AssumedRoleId | String | 34458433936495*** *:alice | The ID of the temporary identity that you use to assume the RAM role. |

**Add Project Object Model (POM) dependencies**

The Alibaba Cloud core library is required. Perform the following steps to add the Alibaba Cloud core library to POM:

```xml
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.aliyun</groupId>
      <artifactId>aliyun-java-sdk-core</artifactId>
      <version>[4.4.9,5.0.0)</version>
    </dependency>
```

```java
        HttpClientConfig clientConfig = HttpClientConfig.getDefault();
        clientConfig.setIgnoreSSLCerts(true);
```

**Error codes**

| HttpCode | Error code | Error message | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | InvalidParameter | The parameter RoleArn is wrongly formed. | The error message returned because the ARN format of the RAM role is invalid. |
| 400 | InvalidParameter.RoleAr n | The parameter RoleArn is wrongly formed. | The error message returned because the ARN format of the RAM role is invalid. |
| 400 | InvalidParameter.RoleS essionName | The parameter RoleSessionName is wrongly formed. | The error message returned because the value of the RoleSessionName parameter is in an invalid format. The value must be 2 to 64 characters in length, and can contain letters, digits, periods (.), at signs (@), hyphens (-), and underscores ( ). _ |
| 400 | InvalidParameter.Durati onSeconds | The Min/Max value of DurationSeconds is 15min/1hr. | The error message returned because the value of the DurationSeconds parameter is invalid. The minimum value is 900, and the maximum value is equal to the value of the MaxSessionDuration parameter. |
| 400 | InvalidParameter.Policy Grammar | The parameter Policy has not passed grammar check. | The error message returned because the syntax of the policy is invalid. |
| 400 | InvalidParameter.Policy Size | The size of Policy must be smaller than 1024 bytes. | The error message returned because the length of the specified policy string exceeds the upper limit. The policy string can be up to 1,024 characters in length. |

| 403 | NoPermission | You are not authorized to do this action. You should be authorized by RAM. | The error message returned because the STS token does not have the required permissions. |
|---|---|---|---|
| 404 | EntityNotExist.Role | The specified Role not exists. | The error message returned because the specified RAM role does not exist. |
| 500 | InternalError | STS Server Internal Error happened. | The error message returned because an internal server error has occurred. |
